name: nom
description: The most widely used Rust parser combinator library; byte- and string-oriented, streaming support

license.comment: Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT"; single license, no dual licensing.

approach.comment: Self-described 'parser combinator framework'; grammar is written as plain Rust functions composed via combinators.

implementation.comment: Only runtime dependency is memchr (pure Rust, default-features disabled); no C/C++ in the tree.

documentation.comment: docs.rs is the primary reference and links the 'Choosing a combinator', error management and recipes guides. The third-party Nominomicon (tfpk.github.io/nominomicon) is linked from the README but targets nom 7.

first-release.comment: crates.io crate created 2015-01-17 (0.1.0); versions list on crates.io begins with 1.0.0-beta in Oct 2015.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 8.0.0 published 2025-01-26. All research reflects nom 8.0.0 (trait-based Parser API, unified Input trait, VerboseError moved to nom-language).

grammar-class.comment: Combinator library; no formal grammar class is imposed (per Assessment Guidelines). Does not document PEG semantics.

grammar-definition.comment: Parsers are ordinary Rust functions/closures; the legacy named!/do_parse! macros were removed in nom 7.

left-recursion.comment: Core nom has no left-recursion support (would recurse infinitely; requires manual rewrite). The first-party nom-language crate (same repo, added with nom 8) provides a precedence module with unary/binary operator precedence and associativity.

ambiguity-handling.comment: alt tries alternatives in order; Err::Error lets the next branch be tried.

backtracking.comment: Unlimited backtracking by default; the cut() combinator turns Err::Error into Err::Failure to commit to a branch.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless: parses &str/&[u8] directly. The Input trait is only implemented for &[u8] and &str; parsing a token slice requires implementing Input for the user's token type.

precedence-pratt-support.comment: Not in the nom crate itself; provided by the first-party nom-language crate (nom_language::precedence) maintained in the nom repository.

unicode-aware.comment: &str input iterates chars (Item = char) and slicing respects char boundaries; the character module offers char-level primitives. Note open issues #1883/#1884 (May 2026) about tag_no_case panicking on Unicode case folds that change byte length.

input-types.comment: Built-in Input impls for &str and &[u8] only; the Input trait (Clone + Sized) is user-implementable for custom stream/token types, e.g. nom_locate's LocatedSpan.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Parallel streaming and complete submodules; streaming variants return Err::Incomplete(Needed) when more data is required.

zero-copy.comment: README: a parser returning a subset of its input returns a slice of that input without copying.

span-tracking.comment: Errors carry the remaining input at the failure point; byte offsets are computed with the Offset trait (impl for str and [u8]). Line/column spans are opt-in via the third-party nom_locate LocatedSpan wrapper (supports nom 8).

output-model.comment: Parsers return arbitrary user types; no generic tree is produced.

semantic-actions.comment: Parser::map, map_res, map_opt, flat_map and the combinator module build values from sub-parser results.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: No implicit skip rules; whitespace is consumed with explicit combinators (character::multispace0, sequence::delimited, the ws recipe).

stateful-parsing.comment: No dedicated state parameter. nom 8 combinators return impl FnMut specifically so closures can capture mutable state; nom_locate's LocatedSpan also carries an 'extra' user field. Borderline: works without wrappers but is not a first-class API.

error-recovery.comment: Parsing stops at the first Err::Error/Err::Failure; no skip-to-sync or user-pluggable recovery API is documented.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: A run yields a single Err; VerboseError accumulates the context chain of one failure path, not multiple independent errors.

expected-token-reporting.comment: Errors carry an ErrorKind naming the combinator that failed (Tag, Digit, ...) and optional context labels, not a set of expected tokens; the docs note VerboseError does not record alternatives tried by alt (nom-supreme's ErrorTree does).

custom-error-types.comment: Error type is a generic parameter; users implement ParseError<I> (plus optional ContextError / FromExternalError).

error-span-fidelity.comment: Errors hold the remaining input (a single failure position, convertible to a byte offset via Offset), not a byte range; convert_error renders line/column for VerboseError<&str>. No labelled secondary spans.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No first-party bridge to ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets; only its own convert_error text renderer (now in nom-language). Third-party crates (nom-supreme, nom_locate) fill the gap.

contextual-error-messages.comment: error::context("label", parser) attaches a static string via the ContextError trait.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Streaming (append-only) input is supported, but there is no tree reuse on edits.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Produces user-defined values; no CST/trivia retention facility.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: The README's 'parsers written with nom' list contains no editor/LSP; no verified rust-analyzer/helix/zed/neovim dependency found (2026-09-19).

runtime-speed-tier.comment: epage/parse-benchmarks-rs JSON benchmark (rustc 1.94.1, results dated 2026-03): nom 8.0.0 parses in 68 ms vs 18 ms for the hand-optimised serde_json baseline (~3.8x) and 27 ms for winnow. Benchmark is maintained by winnow's author; nom lands in the 3-10x bracket. Benchmark checked 2026-09-19.

compile-time-impact.comment: parse-benchmarks-rs reports a 3 s clean debug build for the nom JSON example (vs 1 s winnow, 12 s lalrpop); single small dependency (memchr) and no proc-macros. Incremental delta not separately measured.

allocation-strategy.comment: Zero-copy slices; with the alloc feature disabled nom runs in no_std builds without an allocator (collecting combinators like many0 then need alloc or a custom accumulator).

generated-code-size.comment: Combinator library; no code generation. No source: follows from the approach.

no-std-support.comment: #![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]; works with alloc (default) or fully without an allocator when alloc is disabled.

msrv.comment: rust-version = "1.65.0" for the 8.x series; README states MSRV only changes in major releases (7.x was 1.48).

unsafe-usage.comment: No #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; src/traits.rs contains four small unsafe blocks using str::get_unchecked after boundary checks. Not a full cargo-geiger audit.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: Pure function/trait API; no proc-macro or syn dependency.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: no_std-capable pure Rust with a single pure-Rust dependency and no platform-specific code; not separately verified in nom's CI.

async-friendly.comment: Parsers are plain functions/closures over slices (Send when their captures are); streaming mode with Err::Incomplete is designed for feeding buffers from async I/O. No async API of its own.

github-stars.comment: GitHub shows ~10.5k stars on 2026-09-19 (rounded display value).

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads as of 2026-09-19; lib.rs reports ~35.5k dependent crates.

maintenance-status.comment: Not archived. Last commit 2025-08-26, last release 2025-01-26 (both >12 months before 2026-09-19); 242 open issues and 49 open PRs including unmerged bug fixes from 2025-2026. Fails the 6-month 'actively maintained' bar. winnow is a fork by a former maintainer, not a successor.

documentation-quality.comment: Comprehensive API docs with examples, 'Choosing a combinator', error management and recipes guides, 7-to-8 changelog. The linked Nominomicon tutorial is third-party, targets nom 7 and has unfinished chapters, so not a 5.

tutorial-book.comment: README links the Nominomicon guide and the doc/ tutorials (choosing_a_combinator, error_management, nom_recipes).

notable-users.value: sozu (HTTP proxy), x509-parser and tls-parser (rusticata), pcap-parser
notable-users.comment: Taken from the README's 'parsers written with nom' list; the README also lists many format/protocol parsers.

bus-factor.comment: Geoffroy Couprie (Geal) is the sole owner/primary maintainer; ~99 contributors overall but recent commits are one-off doc/bugfix PRs merged sporadically.
